title: Monodromy and Frobenius Splitting Sieves for the Generalized Fermat Equation x5+y3=z7: An Optimized Small-Prime Local Reduction
content: We study the degree-$7$ Belyi cover \[ \phi(T)=15T^7-35T^6+21T^5 \] that occurs in the Dahmen--Siksek analysis of the generalized Fermat equation \[ x^5+y^3=z^7. \] A central ingredient is a geometric description of the cover. Its branch-cycle passport is \[ (5,1,1),\qquad (3,1,1,1,1),\qquad (7), \] its geometric monodromy group is $A_7$, its arithmetic monodromy group over $\mathbb{Q}(s)$ is $S_7$, and \[ \operatorname{Disc}_T(\phi(T)-s) =-3^6 5^6 7^7 s^4(s-1)^2. \] Thus the sign quotient is the constant quadratic extension $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7})$. The Galois-closure curve is a three-point $A_7$-cover of genus $409$. At every odd prime $\ell\notin\{3,5,7\}$ and every nonbranch parameter $s\in\mathbb{F}_\ell\setminus\{0,1\}$, the Frobenius permutation therefore satisfies the exact parity law \[ (-1)^{7-r(s)}=\left(\frac{-7}{\ell}\right), \] where $r(s)$ is the number of irreducible factors of $\phi(T)-s$ over $\mathbb{F}_\ell$. Consequently the local splitting sieve is naturally a Frobenius-class (Chebotarev) sieve on the thrice-punctured line; the standard function-field Chebotarev theorem gives the corresponding asymptotic class densities. Conditional on Putz's computer-assisted Hunter theorem, we then combine this geometry with the arithmetic analysis of Dahmen--Siksek. In the branch $7\mid y$, Putz's classification and a $7$-adic exclusion of the six pure septic alternatives force the unique exceptional field \[ K_*=\mathbb{Q}(\theta),\qquad \theta^7-483\theta^2+3955\theta-3945=0. \] We give an exact primitive-element certificate proving \[ K_*\cong \mathbb{Q}[T]/(\phi(T)-32/81), \] rather than relying only on the fact that the two models occur in the same earlier arithmetic analysis. Hence the survivor set at a good prime is exactly the locus whose Frobenius cycle type agrees with that of the fixed specialization $32/81$. An exhaustive exact survey of $11\leq\ell\leq 29$ gives the fully separating primes $11,13,17,23,29$; $19$ fails because the $\ell\mid x$ degenerate model has the target splitting type. The triple $\{11,17,29\}$ is the unique triple in this surveyed range simultaneously minimizing the survivor-cardinality product and the survivor-density product. It reduces $3645$ generic nondegenerate CRT combinations to $36$ classes modulo $5423$. The ratio $3645/36=405/4$ may be viewed as finite local bookkeeping only; no probabilistic model for global Diophantine solutions is asserted. We make no claim that the surviving classes are globally realizable, and no characteristic-$7$ residual irreducibility or level-lowering statement is used. The package includes exact rational optimization, two independent finite-field verifiers, an exact field-isomorphism and irreducibility certificate, monodromy checks, and the explicit $36$ CRT residues.
